why: ADOPTED 2026-10-29 (issue 2136): `rclc_executor_add_client_with_request_id(executor, client, response_msg, rclc_client_callback_with_request_id_t)`, rclc's four arguments: `rclc_executor_add_client` whose callback also gets `rmw_request_id_t *request_id`, rclc's `(msg, request_id)` order. `request_id->sequence_number` is the sequence number the request went out under (what the reply was matched on, issue 2009) on every backend; `request_id->writer_guid` is this client's request-writer GUID where the backend reports it through the vtable's new `take_response_with_info` slot (zenoh from the reply attachment, Cyclone DDS from the echoed request header), all zero where it cannot (XRCE-DDS: the Agent owns the request writer). The registration is `rclc_executor_add_client`'s with a second trampoline, carried on the client's arena entry as `request_id_callback` and dispatched in place of the plain callback; `rclc_client_set_response_callback` replaces both, and `rclc_client_call` saves and restores both. ENVELOPE (stated on the declaration): as `rclc_executor_add_client` -- a reply that does not deserialise is dropped without a callback; a descriptor with no response deserialiser is `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED`; the timestamps are not surfaced in C. Test: `packages/api/nros-c/tests/run/typed_service_client.c` (step 5). PRIOR ROW (superseded, declined): ours had one client registration verb and the correlation token belonged to the entity, so a second `add_*` overload was refused; the vtable gave a client no request id to hand over until issue 2136.
